subject: Automotive & EVs
title: California's Zero-Emission Mandate
description: A fast breakdown of California's Zero-Emission Mandate for builders.

hook.text: In 1990, California told automakers: sell zero-emission vehicles or lose access to our market.

buildup.text: The ZEV mandate required 2% of sales to be electric by 1998, rising to 10% by 2003.

discovery.text: Automakers panicked. They lobbied hard and eventually got the mandate weakened significantly.

twist.text: But the mandate planted a seed. It forced companies to invest in EV research they'd otherwise skip.

climax.text: Decades later, California set a 2035 ban on new gas car sales—finishing what the 1990 law started.

punchline.text: One state's rule changed the entire industry's direction.

quiz.question: What did California's 1990 ZEV mandate require?
options: A percentage of zero-emission vehicle sales
